uncertainty: Most per-case core errors are about 0.1%, where closed-loop noise from a single run may be comparable. The training mean shift (+0.0123 pp) and validation mean shift (+0.0035 pp) are small in absolute terms. The consistent overprediction direction in the regressing cases, together with higher |signed drift|/L on both groups, makes a systematic cause more likely than noise.

The broad per-request MAE gain suggests pre_wait captures real precharge timing. The core-error cost may come from applying it too widely: to write bookings, and to precharges bound by tRTP or write recovery as well as tRAS. A narrower version might keep the val3 and MAE gains without the bias; this was not tested.

It is unclear why val7, the dominant ~5% underprediction, gets worse (+0.30 pp) while its request-level signed error rises (+0.0205 -> +0.0237). This points to a closed-loop or coverage interaction that request metrics do not capture.

Training severe tails worsen (reads > 5L +5.7%: gap_sssp 2,205 -> 2,299, arizona 450 -> 496, charlie 454 -> 501, whiskey 213 -> 238, gap_bfs 611 -> 633; whiskey P99.9/L 6.365 -> 6.785). Validation severe tails improve. The two groups disagree on tail direction.

Extreme single reads move both ways: val7 largest overprediction +483 -> +584, val13 largest underprediction -23 -> -78, val14 -2,256 -> -2,297; val4 -941 -> -847, lbm -1,955 -> -1,796. These are individual reads and were not weighted in the decision.

uncertainty: Most per-case core errors are about 0.1%, where closed-loop noise from a single run may be comparable. The training mean shift (+0.0123 pp) and validation mean shift (+0.0035 pp) are small in absolute terms. The consistent overprediction direction in the regressing cases, together with higher |signed drift|/L on both groups, makes a systematic cause more likely than noise.

The broad per-request MAE gain suggests pre_wait captures real precharge timing. The core-error cost may come from applying it too widely: to write bookings, and to precharges bound by tRTP or write recovery as well as tRAS. A narrower version might keep the val3 and MAE gains without the bias; this was not tested.

It is unclear why val7, the dominant ~5% underprediction, gets worse (+0.30 pp) while its request-level signed error rises (+0.0205 -> +0.0237). This points to a closed-loop or coverage interaction that request metrics do not capture.

Training severe tails worsen (reads > 5L +5.7%: gap_sssp 2,205 -> 2,299, arizona 450 -> 496, charlie 454 -> 501, whiskey 213 -> 238, gap_bfs 611 -> 633; whiskey P99.9/L 6.365 -> 6.785). Validation severe tails improve. The two groups disagree on tail direction.

Extreme single reads move both ways: val7 largest overprediction +483 -> +584, val13 largest underprediction -23 -> -78, val14 -2,256 -> -2,297; val4 -941 -> -847, lbm -1,955 -> -1,796. These are individual reads and were not weighted in the decision.

contract_findings: The diff against the incumbent has two parts. (1) pre_wait, declared through p.number with range 0–4, default 0, set to 1: it is added to the precharge slot unless write recovery set the bank's precharge limit. Write recovery is tracked by a new pre_after_write flag, updated in finish_column and slip_after and reset in open_row; finish_column now assigns the limit conditionally instead of taking a max, which is otherwise equivalent. (2) pending_unforced, declared with range 0–1, set to 1: pending_writebacks now also covers write mode entered because the read queue emptied, counting from drain_start, and it applies at read admission only when the buffer is at or above the low watermark.

Each read's completion is computed once in predict() and returned; nothing revises an issued prediction. slip_after moves only the model's own calendar entries and bank limits, which is unchanged from the incumbent.

The inputs are hardware timings and watermarks, the current request's decoded levels, its address (used only to match a buffered write for forwarding, as in the incumbent), and statistics of the model's own past admissions and predictions (write_share EWMA, outstanding reads). I found no use of future requests, oracle completions or internals, workload names, specific addresses or evaluation identities.

No new command scheduler is added. The write-mode replay and its exit hysteresis already exist in the incumbent; pending_unforced only changes an expected count derived from past statistics. The model keeps growing more controller-like, but there is still no per-cycle command selection and no revision of issued predictions, so this is not a demonstrated violation.

Minor code issues, none a contract problem: precharge() does not clear pre_after_write, which is harmless because the bank is then marked precharged and its precharge limit is not consulted; Booking.inserted is set but unused, inherited from the incumbent; source comments say pre_wait was excluded after write recovery because of closed-loop core-cycle results, which is ordinary use of numerical training and validation feedback.

Mechanical integrity: address_mismatch_pairs is 0 and model admissions_without_recorded_latency is 0 in all 28 training and validation cases, and oracle-side unpaired admissions match the incumbent exactly.

Validation mean core error: 0.457919% → 0.445976% (−0.0119 pp, −2.6%). The dominant failure, val7, improves from −5.052% to −4.848% (−0.204 pp, −4.0%), with its reads above 5L 439 → 422. iteration:10:decision.rationale: I found no demonstrated contract violation. The mechanical integrity checks are clean in all 28 cases: address_mismatch_pairs is 0 and model admissions_without_recorded_latency is 0. Oracle-side unpaired admissions are identical to the incumbent's, and matched-read counts move by at most about 200 reads per case, so neither coverage nor cancellation explains the comparison. The candidate changes the incumbent in two ways, and both are declared, bounded parameters. First, pre_wait=1 (range 0–4): a precharge that waits on the bank's tRAS or tRTP limit issues one cycle after that limit. This does not apply when write recovery sets the limit, which the model tracks with a new per-bank pre_after_write flag. Second, pending_unforced=1 (range 0–1): the expected writebacks of reads already in flight also lengthen a write mode that began because the read queue was empty. Both objectives improve on both groups. Core error falls on training (0.0965% to 0.0860%, −0.0105 pp, −10.9%) and on validation (0.4579% to 0.4460%, −0.0119 pp, −2.6%). MAE/L falls on training (0.08484 to 0.08469, −0.18%) and on validation (0.05712 to 0.05521, −3.3%). The worst individual cores improve: val7 goes from −5.052% to −4.848% (−0.204 pp, −4.0%) and lbm from 0.431% to 0.295% (−0.136 pp, −31.5%). Validation tails also improve: P99.9/L −1.3%, the tail metric −1.8%, reads above 5L −2.9% and reads above 1L −1.2%. The improvements are broad. For core error, 8 of 14 training cases and 9 of 14 validation cases improve, and summed gains exceed summed regressions by about 9 times on training and 3 times on validation. For MAE/L, 10 of 14 training cases and 12 of 14 validation cases improve. The costs are real but smaller. val2 core error is about 2.9 times larger (+0.044 pp) and val5 rises 17% (+0.040 pp), both toward overprediction. Validation core error without val7 is +2.7%. Training reads above 5L rise by 59 (+1.4%), and absolute drift/L rises on both groups. The candidate also improves on the rejected iteration-9 pre_wait variant, which worsened core error on both groups. It keeps its roughly 99% core-error and 84–90% MAE/L reduction relative to the stage-entry FixedLat baseline.
uncertainty: The gains are concentrated. lbm supplies nearly all of the training core-error gain (−1.2% without it), val7 all of the validation core-error gain (+2.7% without it), and val5 about 61% of the validation MAE/L gain. Outside these cases the change is roughly neutral on core error.
Each figure comes from a single closed-loop run. Changes of about 0.01 pp in core error or tens of reads in the 5L counts may be within the perturbation noise of closed-loop feedback.

The two mechanisms were evaluated only together, so their contributions are not separated. The val2 and val5 overprediction regressions and the higher drift could come from pending_unforced over-extending write mode in write-heavy phases, or from the one-cycle precharge delay.
val7 remains a −4.8% core-level underprediction and dominates the validation mean. The candidate reduces it but does not address its cause.

The write-recovery exclusion for pre_wait was chosen from closed-loop outcomes, after the unrestricted pre_wait candidate was rejected. That choice carries some tuning risk, although validation core error and MAE/L both improve.
Only single-core cases exist in this stage, so behavior under multicore contention with the new write-mode extension is not measured.
